steps: Derive offset/index/tag partitions before coding. Emit cache and shadow state after every reference and explain each category using seen blocks and shadow membership. If optionally measuring host behavior, identify CPU/tool/counters and put observations in a separate column; do not tune fixture geometry to claim the host matches it.

Reject negative/invalid addresses or zero/non-power-of-two geometry in the general wrapper. Miss penalty is additional to hit cost under this contract; a total-miss-latency input must be converted explicitly.

checks: For .a submit an original hand-traced stream and the N/M/B/D/P model contract. For .b submit all read/write/useful byte totals, ratios and null denominator case. For .c supply actual existing-adapter observations or a clearly labeled denied device-accounting boundary, plus a warm-state explanation and follow-up. The independent Python model checks the bounded policy, not C correctness on every stream or a physical device model.

Reject invalid indices, unknown read/write modes and geometry that violates the stated buffer contract. The empty stream must not divide by zero. A dirty hit does not write back immediately in this policy. A bus transaction, disk I/O and CPU cache fill can have different sizes; replacing one with another invalidates the unit label.

checks: For .a supply both event ledgers, state/lifetime transitions and the chosen native/unavailable route. For .b supply latency/throughput, serial exclusive attribution and the overlapping union example. For .c supply process/thread/elapsed observations and explain the 15>12 case. Reject timestamp reversal within a declared clock, repeated result collection or early buffer reuse. Do not require completion to occur after return for an asynchronous call. checks: For .a provide scripted traces and actual final byte checks, including terminal/zero/retry cases. For .b submit separate native buffered and synchronization samples with file lifetime/warm-state protocol. For .c submit file/device/return-boundary reconciliation and the persistence limits. The independent oracle certifies scripted counts and phase arithmetic only. Native fsync success is evidence of the requested OS boundary, not experimental proof of crash/power-loss durability.

A positive transfer consumes only that many remaining bytes. EINTR in this seam means no bytes transferred by that attempt. Stop terminal EIO and preserve progress; a later successful read cannot erase the error. read returning zero is EOF, while this bounded write adapter treats zero as no progress. Successful write alone is not requested durability; successful file fsync does not prove directory-entry synchronization or survival of every failure mode.

checks: For .a provide scripted traces and actual final byte checks, including terminal/zero/retry cases. For .b submit separate native buffered and synchronization samples with file lifetime/warm-state protocol. For .c submit file/device/return-boundary reconciliation and the persistence limits. The independent oracle certifies scripted counts and phase arithmetic only. Native fsync success is evidence of the requested OS boundary, not experimental proof of crash/power-loss durability.

A positive transfer consumes only that many remaining bytes. EINTR in this seam means no bytes transferred by that attempt. checks: For .a submit the source-backed clock contract, measured resolution and conversion/wrap/error checks. For .b submit raw new pairs, consumed output and all summaries including overhead sensitivity. units.title: Build and inspect: cgroup CPU, memory and I/O accounting

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.

steps: 1. Discover the permitted mount/path and list available/enabled controllers, delegation permissions and inherited limits. Classify every inspected file as policy, counter, gauge or pressure summary.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for cgroup CPU, memory and I/O accounting.

checks: For .a submit the actual hierarchy/controller/delegation inventory or denied record and policy/accounting classification. For .b submit keyed deltas, units, historical-peak treatment and writeback/PSI limits. A reading of memory.peak after reopening an FD is not automatically the requested isolated window.

steps: 1. Read the exact DDI0403E.e DEMCR/DWT scopes and selected-device/core identity. DEMCR at 0xE000EDFC has TRCENA bit 24; DWT_CTRL at 0xE0001000 has NOCYCCNT bit 25/CYCCNTENA bit 0; CYCCNT is at 0xE0001004. Access through the already accepted implementation's MMIO contract. Presence/access/errata/clock are implementation checks, not assumptions from these addresses.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Bare-metal cycle and timer measurement.

checks: For .a supply the manual/device/access/setup ownership checklist and absent/unknown route. For .b derive the 64-cycle case, units, ambiguous-wrap rejection and overhead sensitivity; give an independently justified interval bound for any actual trial. For .c submit the labeled core captured/static certificate and timer/GPIO comparison, or add silicon evidence with all firmware preludes satisfied. No core pass certifies a physical board, energy or WCET. The finite oracle verifies scope flags and arithmetic, not memory-mapped register behavior.

Reject an out-of-width endpoint, nonboolean feature flag, unknown clock or bound admitting a full wrap. The core counter is optional and may be inaccessible; those results must not become zero cycles. Debug state stops CYCCNT, so a halted span cannot be converted into full wall elapsed time. An overhead subtraction at or below overhead is inconclusive. Interrupt cycles, clock changes and probe effects remain in scope unless independently controlled.

steps: 2. Inject the progress script and show the first offset discrepancy in a faulty `off = n` update. Save errno before logging, trace signal disposition, and diagnose a Linux reused-descriptor retry without actually closing an unrelated FD. Repair ownership/cursors, then collect a real supported short-I/O/EOF/SIGPIPE experiment.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for I/O, errno and descriptor failure histories.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. steps: 2. Before opening the withheld oracle, commit predictions, a bounded replay, two hypotheses, first-invalid-state evidence and a repair. Reveal the oracle only after submitting the dossier, replay neighbor/regression cases and request feedback. Repeat after seven days with a different variant; a solo seed must remain unopened until the attempt.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Causal repair, regression and delayed blind transfer.

checks: Submit the nine-field dossier: contract; predictions; replay identities; actual observation; first-invalid-state evidence; competing hypotheses/test; reduced trigger and tri-state certificate; causal repair/limits; regression matrix and transfer. Address all three a/b/c objectives of each linked topic. The static fixture must pass independently, and the learner C must reproduce its intentionally faulty behavior and repaired contract within the declared scope. An unavailable capability keeps its dependent claim open and uses the stated supported alternative; it cannot be reported as a completed diagnostic or physical result. Assessment distinguishes guided fixture replay from a withheld-variant blind attempt.

Reject a mismatched image/input, missing finite bound, invalid adapter result, expired watched object, unsupported tool treated as pass, symptom-only patch, or synthetic value presented as an actual C/tool/hardware observation. Undefined behavior has no promised symptom. Preserve the first cause when later logging/cleanup fails. Tool messages may vary by version; compare semantic evidence rather than exact wording.

steps: 1. State stack direction/interval, ABI, permitted call edges, recursion bound, reentrant callbacks, interrupt nesting and stack selection. Separate MSP/PSP if the actual target uses them.
Before looking at previous source, predict one boundary transition for Stack exhaustion, frames and nested execution.
Produce the smallest independently inspectable implementation or trace for the operation above.
checks: Submit the conditional path bound with unresolved nodes, .su/compiler/object evidence, pattern versus SP comparison, verified child limit setup, native negative and repaired logs, and a separate corruption diagnosis. A watermark, canary or successful run must not be presented as a universal bound. Demonstrate an unseen permitted nesting path or explain the preserved exclusion.

Include an unknown dynamic frame, indirect callee, depth one beyond the supported bound, nested reentrant reporting and extended-frame assumption change. Native recursion has a finite cap and supervisor deadline. Do not lower resource limits in the supervising process or infer stack capacity from an ASan-instrumented image. No corruption or exhaustion need be triggered physically on the board.

steps: 1. Select one prior repaired component and obtain an independently selected variant or trigger, following guide-assessment's withheld-variant process. A self-authored delayed variant is useful additional practice with weaker independence; label it as such and keep the independent unseen criterion open rather than calling it blind or unseen.

checks: Deliver prediction/hypothesis table, minimum trigger, first-invalid-state proof, matching build and bounded observations, focused repair, semantic regression, prevention-versus-mitigation analysis and delayed transfer. A self-authored variant supports delayed practice but does not close independent unseen assessment. Mutex is task-only; raw lock is allowed in all three; ordinary spin lock is allowed in all non-RT contexts and only task context in this restricted RT exercise. Reject out-of-range fields. steps: Implement kl_work for serialized state {queued,running,closed,released}. Events0 submit,1 begin,2 complete,3 close,4 release. Admission fails when closed or occupied; begin transfers queued to running; complete requires running; close is idempotent; release succeeds only once when closed and neither queued nor running. Rejected events preserve state.
Implement the declared core API in src/core.c; compare every supplied fixture and add a discriminating input.
Prove release implies quiescence and closed admission. Compare cancellation return values with work ownership; do not hold a lock required by the worker while synchronously draining it.
checks: A faulty release ignores running work after close; the sentinel release flag demonstrates premature destruction. A deadlock also occurs if teardown waits while holding the worker lock.
All declared CTest cases pass for the learner source, with current source hashes; a scaffold pass is not expected.

steps: Implement kl_grace with events0 enter reader bit id0..7,1 leave,2 retire,3 reclaim. Enter rejects duplicate IDs and admission after retirement; leave requires membership. Retirement is idempotent. Reclaim succeeds only after retirement with no readers and clears retired. This fixed-reader model is intentionally stronger than general RCU and must be mapped critically to the real primitive.

steps: Implement po_sign12(raw) for the low12 bits as a mathematical signed value -2048..2047, ignoring higher bits. Implement po_branch(delta,bits,align) accepting only bits2..30, align2 or4 and aligned signed delta in [-2^(bits-1),2^(bits-1)-align]. steps: Implement lc_program(dst,src,n) on live disjoint octet spans: reject if any new byte requests a0-to-1 transition, leaving all bytes unchanged; otherwise program with bitwise AND. n0 succeeds. This is an atomic admission model, not a claim that physical multi-byte programming is atomic.

steps: Implement lc_select on LCBoot with active and trial slots0/1, confirmed and attempted booleans. If confirmed select active. If unconfirmed and not attempted, select trial and persist attempted1. On later unconfirmed reset select active. Reject invalid fields before output. The model treats attempted persistence as one atomic record; later projects remove that assumption.
Implement the declared core API in src/core.c; compare every supplied fixture and add a discriminating input.
Prove repeated unconfirmed resets eventually return to a known confirmed slot. Identify the exact persistence point before transferring control and the risk if it occurs afterward.
checks: The faulty state machine retries the unconfirmed image forever, causing a boot loop. A watchdog reset alone cannot repair an incorrect persistent selection policy.

Reject wrong count, invalid check or missing marker. Build a minimal firmware crash record producer that writes commit last and never allocates, then cut the model after every store.

steps: Implement cc_token over a nonterminated byte span. Skip ASCII space/newline/tab; recognize decimal0..65535(kind1), x(2), ((3), )(4), +(5), *(6), and end(0). Return1 on token/end,0 on invalid or overflow. On failure preserve offset/kind/value. On success set value0 except constants. Do not call strtol or a lexer library.

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.
requires_reasons.LAB-LI-01B: Explicit project contract consumes the prior Vectored partial progress capability.

steps: Implement li_ready_after(result,budget_exhausted) for a synthetic read result: positive progress retains readiness, -2 means EAGAIN and clears readiness,0 EOF clears readiness,-1 terminal error clears readiness. Return1 while progress remains, even when a dispatch budget was exhausted. Exercise the actual anonymous-pipe EPOLLET adapter and compare drain-to-EAGAIN with a local ready queue.
Implement the declared core API in src/core.c; compare every supplied fixture and add a discriminating input.
Distinguish kernel notification, locally remembered readiness and actual EAGAIN. Derive a fairness budget that does not lose readiness or spin forever after EOF.

All declared CTest cases pass for the learner source, with current source hashes; a scaffold pass is not expected.

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.
requires_reasons.LAB-LI-02B: Explicit project contract consumes the prior Edge readiness and fair draining capability.

steps: Implement li_slot(head,tail,capacity,out) for uint32_t monotonic counters: capacity is a power of two in1..2^30, unsigned tail-head must be<capacity, and output is tail&(capacity-1). Reject invalid/full states unchanged. Then map the arithmetic to raw io_uring offsets and acquire/release operations after feature probing.
Implement the declared core API in src/core.c; compare every supplied fixture and add a discriminating input.
Derive the bounded-distance interpretation under counter wrap. Separate single-producer ownership, ring-slot lifetime and payload-before-tail publication.
checks: A producer masks tail and overwrites a still-owned full slot. Adding a barrier cannot repair missing capacity admission.
All declared CTest cases pass for the learner source, with current source hashes; a scaffold pass is not expected.

Compare with the supplied faulty teaching path that validates only the32-byte physical extent; attacker controls offset/n/data and harmless success is sentinel change.

requires_reasons.LAB-NS-07B: Explicit project contract consumes the prior Saturating lanes and scalar tails capability.

steps: Implement ns_close(actual,expected,atol,rtol) for finite values and finite tolerances with0<=atol and0<=rtol<=1. Use the mathematical target |actual-expected|<=atol+rtol*|expected| and define actual admission by the supplied rounded scaled comparison (boundary rounding is part of this contract), scaling to avoid overflow in difference or threshold. NaN and infinities are rejected, including equal infinities. This is an admission predicate, not proof of an algorithm error bound.
Implement the declared core API in src/core.c; compare every supplied fixture and add a discriminating input.

Derive the asymmetric expected-relative policy, near-zero behavior and exceptional-value handling. Explain rounding at the acceptance boundary and why a tolerance must come from a prior requirement or error analysis.
checks: The mutant removes the absolute component, rejecting a permitted near-zero error. Conversely a loose tolerance selected after seeing failures can hide a wrong algorithm.
All declared CTest cases pass for the learner source, with current source hashes; a scaffold pass is not expected.

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-ER-02: Which representation preserves every required optional payload? Compare explicit tag and uint32 payload versus zero-reserved niche. Present zero, UINT32_MAX and an absent value distinguish the admitted states; measure layout only after equalizing the contract.
Derive the state cardinality of tagged versus zero-reserved optional values, including the lost present-zero state and valid result payload selection.
Implement total constructors and checked accessors while preserving output on rejected niche construction; do not copy uninitialized union members or compare padding.
checks: Packing (value=0,present=1) into an output initially 91 rejects with 91 unchanged; (17,0) stores zero; UINT32_MAX is a valid present value. Unpacking zero produces ER_ABSENT. The full tagged alternative must distinguish absent from present zero.

Enumerate the reduced 8-bit model independently, then test actual UINT32_MAX and invalid discriminants. Measure sizeof and alignment on two available data models; a missing model is unavailable evidence. Kill premature-output-write and absence-uses-payload mutants.

readings.purpose: Compare explicit result representation and lazy failure propagation with the C implementation.
Bound niche optimization claims and optional-value composition to the documented cases.
Require explicit diagnostic modes and valid nonlocal-jump/cleanup boundaries.
Compare automatic language destruction and partial initialization with explicit C cleanup.

steps: Explain which failure stage owns the error offset, and why early-return propagation is not transaction rollback or automatic cleanup.
Implement strict checked accumulation and two single-evaluation propagation forms without statement expressions, strto* or parser libraries.
checks: 1:65534 succeeds with 65535. 65536:0 fails RANGE at offset4; 1:2x fails INVALID at3; 1: fails at2; :1 fails at0. 1:65535 fails RANGE at7 and must not publish the first field.

Generate all strings of length0–6 over digits0,1,9,colon,x and compare with an independent grammar/integer model. Add UINT32 bounds and long zero prefixes. Record callback/expression counters to kill double evaluation and retain a canary output for every rejection; kill premature publication and trailing-input acceptance mutants.

steps: Separate ownership transfer, physical byte copying, source poisoning and diagnostic enforcement; explain why ISO C17 cannot prevent all implicit copies of this public struct.
Implement checked move/consume operations and an isolated diagnostic probe that intentionally ignores OW_MUST_USE, with extension-enabled and portable builds reported separately.
checks: After moving three blocks, destination.count=3 and source.count=0. Consuming the source returns DEAD; consuming the destination releases three blocks once; a second consume returns DEAD. A direct C assignment copying the original owner is a counterexample to an alleged static move-only guarantee.

Test self-move, occupied destination, empty source, repeated consumption and allocator release counts. Reject the source-not-poisoned mutant. Compile a copied owner without consuming both copies: use it as a static counterexample, not an unbounded double-free experiment. Record whether GCC/Clang actually emit the ignored-result diagnostic.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-OW-08: Should the component dynamically track range loans or rely on a whole-object ownership protocol? Compare four-slot range guard registry versus single exclusive owner with documented temporary borrows. A split writer and two disjoint mutable views must be admitted while an overlapping reader is rejected; compare metadata, checks and exhaustion behavior under that same contract.
Derive reader/writer interval exclusion separately from pointer lifetime, then explain finite identity exhaustion and why a runtime token does not prevent illicit raw aliases.
Implement bounded acquire/release and transactional writer splitting with arithmetic-safe extent checks, generation retirement and an explicit guard ownership rule.
checks: A writer[0,8) blocks a reader[3,4). Splitting it at3 creates[0,3) and[3,8), invalidates the parent token and admits no gap or overlap. A writer[8,8) may coexist because it touches no element. A released token cannot release a later loan in the same slot.

Use an independent finite-set intersection oracle for all small extents/ranges/read-write combinations, then test SIZE_MAX bounds and UINT32_MAX serial retirement. Exhaust the slot table before split and compare complete pre/post books and output canaries. Kill the conflict-check omission mutant; explain that reduced exhaustive checks do not prove arbitrary C lifetimes.

steps: Prove the distinct value/control lifetimes, no-resurrection property and count-overflow behavior; distinguish reference-count synchronization from pointee synchronization and cycle collection.

Implement strong/weak ownership twice, first under exclusion and then with C17 atomics, documenting initialization publication, owned-reference preconditions, callback effects and each memory-order edge.
checks: Downgrade, retain, drop, drop yields strong0,weak1, one value destruction and no control reclamation. Upgrade now fails DEAD. Dropping the remaining weak reclaims the control once. Four threads each retain/drop5000 times while holding their own strong reference; after all owned strong references end, destruction occurs once, and a retained weak keeps the control available for a failed upgrade.

Trace every strong/weak boundary with an independent counter model, test maximum-count refusal, and reject omission of the implicit weak release. Run the actual four-thread anchor, separate TSan if available, GCC/Clang optimized and ASan/UBSan builds, inspect atomic lowering and report lock-free status. A quiet race detector does not prove the memory-order argument or reclaim safety for fabricated references.

Implement fail-at-N, counting and poisoning as the accepted containers.array allocator callback adapter, preserving typed storage legality and explicit finite-capacity behavior.
checks: Take16 succeeds; fail-at2 makes take1 return null. Live1,peak1,attempts2. Release poisons all16 requested elements, gives live0/releases1; a second release only records an invalid-release event. Starting attempts at SIZE_MAX refuses allocation and leaves it at SIZE_MAX.

Sweep every allocation failure point of frontier and COW workloads, fill all eight slots, test sizes0/16/17 and counter extrema, and verify requested-prefix poison plus release accounting. Compare the imported header byte for byte with the accepted ABI and reject the no-poison mutant. Integrate with the learner dynamic array and T65 error paths, measuring actual calls rather than inferring zero allocation from source spelling.

steps: Derive the integer-wrap admission defect, attacker-controlled transition and exact violated authority property; distinguish a checked trusted-core boundary from whole-process memory safety.

Implement the subtraction-based boundary check, unchanged-on-failure behavior and an internal validated descriptor, preserving the simple core while documenting every remaining caller and same-process assumption.
checks: With 32-bit unsigned, offset=UINT_MAX-3,count8,value7 passes the flawed wrapped check and changes tenant1 indices12..15 from99 to7. The repaired API returns INVALID and leaves both tenants unchanged. This is a bounded integrity-property violation in original teaching code, not an out-of-bounds C access.

Run the local cross-tenant demonstration with synthetic canaries, compare flawed/repaired outcomes, enumerate all ordinary tenant/offset/count combinations around8 and test UINT_MAX wrap cases. Reject the flawed-check mutant by a normal semantic assertion. Explain why ASan may remain quiet: every actual array access is in bounds. Test mitigation regression without claiming arbitrary code execution or privilege escalation.

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-AD-02: Should unknown advisory packet variants be rejected or preserved as exact borrowed bytes? Compare closed validated sum versus open sum with retained unknown bytes. Round-trip an unrecognized synthetic variant through a version1relay and test whether version2recovers it without weakening critical-tag rejection.

Derive product versus sum cardinality and distinguish a C union representation from an automatically checked discriminated union; show why -Wswitch-enum is a diagnostic policy, not an ISO C exhaustiveness theorem.

Draw all admitted tag/payload states, establish uint64 sufficiency for two uint32 values, and explain which inactive-member operations are avoided. Derive a counterexample to the claim that adding a default branch makes future variants exhaustively handled. Compare Rust enum constructors and binding behavior with C aggregate initialization and private-header discipline.
checks: PAIR(UINT32_MAX,5) measures4294967300; NUMBER(0) is distinct from EMPTY despite equal measurement. Invalid tag99 leaves prior result unchanged. A PAIR requested as NUMBER leaves its output sentinel untouched.

Run adt.sums and compile the missing-enumerator probe with -Wswitch-enum -Werror. Both semantic mutants must fail: omitted second product member and silently accepted invalid tag. Add every variant and invalid boundary, inspect enum size without assuming it is the wire tag size, and compare debug/release generated branches.

steps: Distinguish a set of independent options from a mutually exclusive sum, and explain why reserved bits must be rejected or retained under a documented evolution policy rather than silently cleared.

steps: Derive a UTF-8 validation predicate from RFC3629 and explain why successful construction proves byte encoding only while the backing bytes remain live and unchanged.

Track input position and remaining continuation count without forming an out-of-range pointer. For each sequence derive minimum scalar value and maximum scalar value; compare scalar count with byte count. State storage lifetime and mutation restrictions explicitly, including a safe constructed example where another alias changes a previously validated buffer.

Run adt.text and the Python strict UTF-8 differential oracle for all one/two-byte strings plus specified three/four-byte boundary samples. Kill overlong and surrogate acceptance mutants. Record that Python decoding is an independent implementation, not a proof of normalization or all higher-level text properties.

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.
requires_reasons.U-T16-03-03: Import memory.pool: Typed fixed storage, bounded exhaustion and generation-checked handles; no stale identity reuse.
requires_reasons.LAB-AD-08: Explicit project contract consumes the prior UTF-8 smart constructors and validated borrowed text capability.

steps: Separate nominal handle category, pool identity, slot generation and ownership; demonstrate why a C wrapper cannot create a compile-time fresh brand per runtime pool or enforce linear use.

Derive FREE/LIVE/RETIRED transitions and count available slots. Explain why copying a handle is permitted by C yet does not duplicate ownership. Pool objects must remain live at fixed addresses and cannot be reinitialized or reused while handles survive: pointer identity does not prevent ABA across object lifetimes. Compare PhantomData nominal/lifetime roles without claiming equivalent static checks.
checks: A handle frompoolA is rejected bypoolB; release/reacquire invalidates the old generation; release atUINT_MAX retires its slot and reduces usable capacity to3.

Run adt.brands and enumerate short acquire/release/get traces against an independent occupancy/generation model. Kill owner-check omission and generation-check omission independently. Compile a wrong-category handle probe; show that copying or explicitly constructing a valid public representation bypasses any unforgeability claim.

steps: Derive required backing extent from shape and strides, including empty shapes and overflow, and distinguish a read-only overlapping view from a mutable injective layout.

steps: Derive acyclicity from a topological child-index invariant and explain when a checked arena can support unchecked internal traversal without allowing later mutation to invalidate the proof.

Run adt.arena and independent postfix/tree evaluation cases. Kill forward-reference acceptance and arithmetic-overflow omission. Add unreachable malformed nodes, multiple roots, shared children, empty and maximum count, then record stack-use output.

steps: Derive lens get-put, put-get and put-put laws and prism review/preview round trips; explain how lawful optics differ from arbitrary field mutation helpers.

Write each law as an executable predicate and derive which information an update may change. Compare the C functions with the inspected lens type laws; C types do not enforce those laws. Distinguish field equality from raw struct memcmp because padding need not encode semantic identity.
checks: Setting x of(1,2)to3 gives(3,2); setting it toitscurrent1 preserves bothfields. Preview(review(3))=3; preview(EMPTY)fails without publishing0.

Run adt.optics:256combinations assess get-put/put-get/put-put and prism round trips. Kill the collateral-y-write and EMPTY-as-NUMBER mutants. Add composition of nested pairs, identify a law violated by a clamping setter, and explain why exhaustive small domains are not proof for arbitrary callback optics.

steps: Distinguish tolerance from permissiveness: an unknown noncritical alternative can be retained exactly, while malformed known alternatives and unknown required semantics must fail.

Define a sum of known-number, known-empty and unknown bytes; retain tag and payload even when semantics are unavailable. State lifetime, disjointness, maximum255payloadbytes and overflow-free size calculation. Compare binary unknown-field preservation with the inspected Protobuf guide and demonstrate a field-wise rebuilding path that loses unknown data.
checks: 09 03 04 05 06 round-trips byte-for-byte;01 01 07 fails as malformed known data;80 00 fails as unsupported required semantics.

Run adt.evolution and construct a two-version relay trace. Kill unknown-payload-discard and malformed-known-acceptance mutants. Test all truncation points, trailing bytes, capacity shortages, zero-length unknown payload and borrowed-buffer mutation. Record which operations preserve unknown data and which deliberately reject it.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-MP-02: Should the packet schema use a generated typed interface or a runtime field-descriptor interpreter? Compare typed X-macro-generated operations versus runtime descriptor-driven operations. Add a field and compare stale-consumer detection, generated text size and runtime dispatch under the same validation and wire contract.

Explain how repeated template-header inclusion generates distinct typed functions, how associated element/ring types must agree, and why token substitution has no trait-implementation proof or automatic instantiation isolation.

Derive head<count/capacity invariants, occupied logical slots and output ownership. Compare generated specialization with Rust generic/associated-type obligations and show a mismatched ring/element instantiation diagnosed by C. Explain why a template include guard would silently suppress the second instantiation and why internal macro names can collide.
checks: Push0..3, pop0, push4, then pop1..4. Both scalar and pair instances preserve every semantic field. Full/empty operations leave their designated output/control state unchanged.

Run metaprog.mono and inspect preprocessed two-instance source. Kill incorrect-tail-index and stationary-head mutants. Compile and link two translation units using declarations to detect accidental multiple definitions; record generated symbol count and text size separately from handwritten equivalents under the same capacity/failure contract.

steps: Separate a required C constraint diagnostic, a chosen -Werror rejection, and a runtime range guard; show which properties constant-size generic storage can check before execution.

Derive count<=SIZE_MAX/width before multiplication and the independent budget bound. Explain why C17 _Static_assert requires an integer constant expression, VLA support differs from fixed arrays, and syntactically valid macros do not impose an abstract trait. Compare the inspected Rust const-generic type/use restrictions without claiming arbitrary compile-time evaluation equivalence.
checks: count4,width8,limit32 yields32;limit31fails. SIZE_MAX*2 fails before overflow; count0 or width0 is outside this storage contract.

Run metaprog.constraints and compile the negative constraint probes expecting a named diagnostic, not a link failure. Kill multiplication-overflow omission and storage-budget omission independently. Test size_t-width changes analytically and inspect whether published C23 wording is available before attributing a C2x compiler behavior to the standard.

steps: Explain the equality-implies-equal-hash law, why cached/nonsemantic fields must be excluded consistently, and what deterministic generation plus shrinking establishes and leaves unproved.

Prove reflexivity/symmetry/transitivity obligations separately from hashing and collisions. Specify FNV parameters and unsigned64 wrap; this is not a cryptographic integrity claim. The shrinking order finds a local minimum under decrement moves, not necessarily a globally simplest witness for arbitrary nonmonotone predicates. Callback/context must remain live, deterministic and side-effect controlled.
checks: Keys(1,2,cache0) and(1,2,cache9) compareequal and hash equally; (1,3,0) differs. Propertyx+y<5 over0..8 yields a failing pair ofsum5. Reflexivity finds no failure in the bounded domain.

Run metaprog.laws, independently recompute canonical hashes and enumerate bounded law triples. Kill equality-ignores-y and hash-includes-cache mutants. Inject a deliberately wrong equality/hash callback through the learner testing.faults adapter and retain a minimized witness; explain why equal hashes do not imply equal keys.

steps: Distinguish compile-time argument-category checking from compile-time parsing of an arbitrary format string, and prove bounded sink failure does not publish partial output.

Derive the10digit bound for UINT32_MAX and reverse temporary digits only after capacity admission. For text, prove scan stops on insufficient capacity without publishing a prefix. Compare C++ basic_format_string constant-evaluation compatibility with this narrower C factory: it enforces argument categories, not arbitrary formatting grammar or backing lifetime.
checks: Appenduint32zero yieldsbyte30; appendliteral%n yieldspercent/n, with no conversion interpretation. Appending4294967295 to a sink with9freebytes fails unchanged; with10freebytes writes exactly10digits.

Run metaprog.formatting, compile an unsupported MP_ARG category probe, and test every capacity0..11. Kill failure-used-count modification and zero-as-empty-output mutants. Compare against an independent decimal-string oracle and a guard-filled output suffix; distinguish valid text termination preconditions from bound checking.

checks: A borrowed int7 measures7. A callback returning DS_FAILED after writing123 into its private output leaves caller output99 unchanged. A missing table rejects before invocation. The wrong-return-type callback fixture must fail strict C17 compilation.

steps: Separate capture-by-value/reference from invocation capabilities and explain the documented Rust rule that move capture alone does not imply only FnOnce.
Implement the three explicit modes with checked arithmetic, exactly-once consumption and clear borrowed/owned capture lifetimes; add borrowed-slice and owning-resource closures.
checks: Capture3 shared calls with2 return5 repeatedly without capture mutation. Mutable calls return5 then7. Once capture1 with2 returns3 and later DS_EMPTY. Once INT_MAX with1 returns DS_RANGE with unchanged output and becomes inactive.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-DS-10: Which callable representation matches retention and movement requirements? Compare borrowed immediate function reference versus owning byte-encoded small capture versus owning typed heap capture. Escaping retention, self pointers, alignment, destruction and allocation failure distinguish contracts before dispatch timing.
Derive erased-call representation, invocation thunk, ownership and empty states; distinguish byte encoding from placing an arbitrary typed object in character storage.
Implement capture construction, explicit movement and no-fail destruction through dod.small_buffer with no duplicated allocator logic, including a spill and failure rollback.
checks: Capture byte7 called with3 produces10. Move leaves the source inactive/empty and destination active. Dropping source then destination twice invokes the resource destructor exactly once. Allocation failure during a large capture assignment leaves the destination empty and ownership with the caller.

Drive assign/call/move/drop traces through a logical ownership model and an allocator request/release log. Exercise inline16 versus spill17 and capture128 versus129 using thunks that accept those schemas. Compile with sanitizers, but diagnose ownership-state errors before invoking an inactive or mismatched thunk. Count bytes copied, allocations, owner size, dispatch and destructors under the13-dimension contract.

steps: State the authority graph, permitted attacker actions and property: delegated rights remain a subset and revoked epochs cannot authorize a new effect. Distinguish a cooperative token from an unforgeable capability.
Implement subset admission, owner/epoch validation, bounded revocation and checked effect publication without global ambient authority.
checks: A full-rights capability can add5. Its attenuated read-only capability cannot change the counter. Attempting to attenuate read-only rights to full rights rejects with output unchanged. After revocation, the former full capability returns stale and the counter remains5.

Enumerate rights0–3 and all subset/non-subset requests. Retain capabilities through each revoke and retirement, comparing the counter and status to an independent set/epoch model. Mutation1 permits amplification; mutation2 accepts a stale epoch. Success is an observable synthetic counter change contrary to the declared policy, not a crash or privilege escalation. Repairs require both rejection and preserved state.

readings.purpose: The attacker perspective reveals whether a token is actually authoritative or simply trusted data. A subset check is meaningful only under a threat model that prevents the caller from changing the checked authority metadata.

State the authority graph, permitted attacker actions and property: delegated rights remain a subset and revoked epochs cannot authorize a new effect. Distinguish a cooperative token from an unforgeable capability.
deliverables: Implement the original DSAuthority/DSCapability model over a synthetic int counter. Rights bits1(read) and2(add), owner identity and finite epochs enforce checked API requests. Issue and attenuation must never add rights; add requires both root and capability permission; revoke invalidates old epochs and retires after3. Attack only this cooperative local model by requesting a stronger mask, reusing a revoked capability and crossing owners. Then analyze a C client that directly forges exposed fields: explain why this violates the model and refutes a broader security claim. Design an opaque broker/process boundary that can enforce the stronger threat model.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-DO-04: Which inline representation supports the actual capture contract? Compare counted byte encoding versus concrete typed union versus heap-owned typed capture. Byte arrays do not establish arbitrary typed object access; self-referential and owning captures require a relocation/ownership rule.

Derive the representation invariant for empty, inline and heap states and the exact invalidation events for borrowed views; explain why alignment of a character array alone does not permit arbitrary typed C objects.
Implement all capacity transitions and a fixed-capacity alternative using allocator injection, with strong append rejection and exactly-once resource release under move/reset.
checks: Appending16 bytes performs no allocation. A failed17th byte preserves length16 and all bytes. Successful spill followed by move leaves the source empty and transfers exactly one allocation. Truncating to8 and compacting frees that allocation once; resetting both owners performs no second free.

Run an operation-model generator over append lengths0,1,15,16,17,127,128,129; truncate, compact, move and reset. Preserve operation traces and independent byte-list state. Inject allocator failure at every spill and verify live allocation ownership, exact release counts and output state separately from callback instrumentation. Compile without a container/string library. Record sizeof/_Alignof on each available target. The header intentionally exposes fields for teaching, so forged state is outside the checked API contract and must be discussed.

steps: Derive low7-bit addition, high-bit combination and saturation masks, proving which intermediate carries can occur and why neighboring lanes remain independent.
Implement the unsigned SWAR expression and an independent scalar oracle without relying on char signedness, endian memory reinterpretation or vector extensions.
checks: 0xff00ff00 plus0x01010101 produces0xff01ff01. A255+1 low lane must saturate without adding1 to the adjacent lane. Every pair of byte inputs must agree with min(255,a+b).

The supplied anchor exhausts65,536 pairs repeated across lanes and placed into each isolated lane. Extend the oracle with all neighbor lane boundaries0,127,128,255 around each active pair and100,000 seeded mixed words. Record that the exhaustive dimension is the single-lane value pair, not all2^64 word pairs. Inspect shifts against width and integer promotions. Compare little- and big-endian serialization separately from numerical results.

readings.purpose: Ordinary word addition is not lane-wise addition; carries and saturation require a proof. A benchmark over only identical lanes can miss a carry leaking into a different neighboring lane.

The packed numerical lane convention is independent of how a uint32_t is stored as bytes.

steps: Derive entity-to-table/row and table-row-to-entity invariants, query mask semantics and the distinction between stable entity ID and invalidated row references.

Implement migration with destination admission before source removal, swap-row repair and transactional query updates; implement required/excluded-mask query selection and versioned cache invalidation.
checks: Create entity0/1 in mask1 and entity2 in mask3. Moving0 into mask3 succeeds and moves1 to row0 of mask1. Moving1 into now-full mask3 rejects without deleting it. Step changes both-component positions30,10 with velocities2,1 into32,11; a later overflow preserves the whole table.

Enumerate all legal entity/mask requests for bounded traces up to length6, compare masks and active values with a dictionary oracle and check both mapping directions after every step. Explicitly test self-migration, last-row removal, destination full and overflow at each visited row. For cache tests, distinguish a changed set of matching tables from changed rows within an existing table. Benchmark equal query results with a scalar dictionary and include structural edits in the workload.

steps: Derive persistence as multiple observable versions with shared immutable subgraphs, distinguishing it from durable storage and from a mutable object with a const pointer.
Implement leaf-to-root path copying, an explicit zipper reconstruction and failure rollback without mutating published nodes; state allocator ownership and snapshot lifetime.
checks: Updating root0 cell3=17 creates4 nodes; updating that root cell6=29 creates4 more. The first root still reads cell6=0. Each of the four allocation-failure ordinals rejects with the output root and previously reachable nodes unchanged.

For update sequences of length0–5 over indices0,3,7 and values0,1,-1 compare every retained version with a copied8-element Python/list model. Traverse nodes independently to count reachability and shared edges; reject cycles or depth errors. Run each allocation failure ordinal. Test zipper root/leaf moves and reconstruction equality, including returning to the original snapshot. Report measured allocation/retention and not merely O(log n); for the bounded trie exactly4 nodes/update is independently expected.

readings.locator: Why Would I Want This?: structural sharing and workload tradeoffs
readings.purpose: Cheap root copying shifts costs into path cloning and retained history. Const qualification does not freeze aliases, and a path-copy algorithm that silently mutates one old node breaks every older version sharing it.

The zipper may borrow a live arena and immutable root, but never retain raw pointers across arena reset. Implement a reachability census over a chosen root set and compare region reset with a separately specified reference-count reclamation design, including rollback if construction fails.

steps: Derive bitmap rank as the population count of preceding bits and prove compact-child count/order invariants; distinguish trie-prefix, full-hash and actual-key equality.

checks: Keys1 and17 deliberately share the full4-bit hash but retain values10 and20. Updating17 to88 in a new root leaves20 in the old root. Inserting key0 changes bitmap rank and must not make key1 unreachable. Each of3 allocation failure points preserves old snapshots.

Generate every key pair and both insertion orders, then update and delete either member while retaining all roots. Add triplets selecting low chunks0,1,3 and full-hash pair0/16; compare flattening to sorted key/value pairs from a dictionary. For every node recompute count and rank independently; test pool exhaustion. Public reference implements lookup/update only: submitted deletion and its failure/normalization evidence are separately required and remain unexecuted in the author campaign.

steps: Prove ordered-DAG sequence semantics, cached length consistency and ownership of shared leaves; distinguish byte, codepoint, grapheme and line coordinates.

checks: Leaves ab and cd concatenate to abcd; concatenating that root with itself flattens to abcdabcd while the ab leaf remains ab. Capacity7 rejects an8-byte flatten without touching the output canary or written. An empty leaf returns root0.

Generate edit traces length0–5 over insert empty/a/ab/NUL, delete zero/one/all and each boundary position, comparing byte sequences after every step. Check invalid positions and capacity exhaustion preserve state. Independently traverse the DAG to verify cached lengths, older-node edges and sharing; flatten must visit logical occurrences, not each unique node once. Construct left-deep concatenation to measure depth and compare balanced rebuild. The author anchor covers concat/flatten; split, balance, gap and piece implementations require their own submitted evidence and are not counted executed by that anchor.

deliverables: Implement the DRope leaf/concat/flatten anchor with64 typed nodes, leaf length0–8 and maximum expanded length128. Apply the same edit scripts to all three and a flat byte-list oracle. No Unicode scalar, grapheme or line-number equivalence is implied by byte offsets.

steps: Explain readiness as a hint, partial progress as frame state, and registration/quiescence lifetime; distinguish this model from completion submission rings and automatic Rust Future pinning.

steps: Explain scope-owned task lifetime, failure aggregation and cooperative cancellation, including why a cancellation flag does not establish completion or a bounded join latency.

Derive admission/closing/quiescent states, implement spawn/join and deterministic error selection, then compose with the existing work.pool artifact without detached tasks or prematurely released contexts.
checks: Spawn result5 then result0: after join, both slots are joined, cancellation is true and result is5. Fail admission at attempt2: exactly one child remains admitted, its context is retained until join and no second thread handle is joined. An uncooperative infinite child is a bounded external-timeout experiment, not silently declared cancelled.

Inject failure before every admission, record thread/context ownership, join zero/one/eight children, reject ninth admission and late spawn. Use a barrier-controlled failure with siblings acknowledging cancellation and compare accepted/completed counts. Reject both missing-cancellation and swallowed-result mutants. Run separate TSan and demonstrate that eventual cancellation needs child checkpoints.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-SC-04: Should multi-channel selection use a shared registration lock or separate channel locks? Compare one shared hub mutex and predicate versus per-channel mutexes plus a registration/recheck protocol. Publish between the final empty observation and waiter registration; require no lost notification and exact close/cancel ownership under both implementations.

Derive readiness, linearization, close/drain and cancellation semantics; compare deterministic selection with Go ready-case randomness and distinguish rendezvous acknowledgment from merely enqueuing an offer.

Implement buffered/rendezvous operations and select with a single predicate-registration boundary, explicit spurious-wakeup loops, finite tickets and quiescent destruction; retain coroutine frames until generation-specific disarm.
checks: Capacity2: send7,close,send8 gives OK,OK,CLOSED; the first receive returns7 and the next CLOSED. Two ready channels alternate preference. A capacity0 sender of42 returns OK only after select consumes42. Close before acknowledgment returns CLOSED to sender; an acknowledged send remains successful if cancellation arrives before sender resumes.

Test full/empty, both ready, one closed, all closed, close with buffered values, cancellation with blocked sender/receiver and accepted-versus-unaccepted rendezvous. Repeatedly inject spurious broadcasts. Capture event histories and verify no lost/duplicated accepted values. Reject send-after-close and skipped-buffer mutants; independently model sequential traces and use TSan for actual threads.

steps: Separate sender recipe, connected operation storage, start permission and completion ownership; identify the dated C++ proposal guarantees that an exposed C struct does not enforce.
Implement the serialized state protocol and backend lifetime adapter, including synchronous completion, cancellation races, callback reentrancy policy and exactly-once terminal release.
checks: Complete before start is INVALID. Start then stop leaves STARTED with cancellation requested. Complete CANCELLED,3 invokes one receiver and reaches DONE. Duplicate complete on a still-live test state is INVALID and leaves callback count1. A separate heap-owned completion test frees the state inside its receiver without later access.

Enumerate invalid start/complete orders, value/error/stopped alternatives and cancellation-before-completion. Use a receiver that frees a heap state to detect post-callback access under ASan. Reject duplicate-completion and cancel-as-completion mutants. For a concurrent adapter, use one atomic winner and demonstrate that losers never inspect reclaimed storage without their own retained reference.

steps: Identify linearization and ownership in owner/thief races, last-item arbitration, finite-index exhaustion and stale slot reads; distinguish SC correctness from weak-order proof and actual lock-free progress.
Derive a circular representation with monotonic nonwrapping indices and atomic slots; implement push/pop/steal with a proof for empty, full, last-item and reused-slot states.
checks: Push7,push8,pop,steal,steal returns OK,OK,8,7,EMPTY. Eight live entries fill capacity and a ninth push leaves state unchanged. Empty pop preserves its output canary. Starting quiescent top=bottom=SIZE_MAX-1 makes push return OVERFLOW. Two thieves plus owner process4000 distinct IDs exactly once in the supplied threaded anchor.

Differentially compare1095 bounded sequential traces with Python deque, include repeated empty pops and capacity reuse, record concurrent invocation/response histories and check small histories for legal linearizations. Reject wrong-pop and omitted-steal-CAS mutants. Run TSan, inspect generated instructions and report atomic_is_lock_free; do not infer weak-memory correctness from x86 stress.

steps: Derive snapshot validation, write-set locking, abort restoration and the distinction between transaction isolation, atomic C accesses and memory reclamation; explain inconsistent-read hazards before commit.

Implement bounded read/write sets, read-your-writes, nonblocking lock acquisition and validated commit using the declared SC baseline; prove failed commits leave payload unchanged while allowing timestamp gaps.
checks: TransactionA starts, B writes cell0=7 and commits: A reading cell0 returns CONFLICT without changing output99. If A reads7 before B commits8, then stages cell1=9, A commit conflicts and cell1 remains0 with its lock clear. Two concurrent increment transactions over two equal cells produce2000 committed increments and never expose unequal admitted reads.

Force conflict before a read, after a read and during partial lock acquisition; test repeated writes, empty/read-only transactions and timestamp exhaustion. Reject missing read validation and missing commit validation mutants. Use an independent serial-history model for small schedules, TSan for actual threads and fault hooks for every commit phase. Explain why atomic individual loads alone do not provide a coherent transaction.

Implement timestamped publication, exact pin identity, visible-version selection and reclamation with a bounded-space proof under the four-reader assumption.
checks: PinA at[0,0], publish[1,2], publish[3,4]: A still reads[0,0]. DropA and reuse its pin slot forB: old handleA is STALE and B reads[3,4]. A clock at UINT64_MAX refuses publish. Snapshot visibility is repeatable for the two-field value; no multi-object serializability or durability is claimed.

Enumerate pin/publish/read/drop traces against an independent immutable-history model, test four pins at different versions and a fifth refusal, stale slot reuse and generation retirement. Reject pin-ignorant collection and missing-generation mutants. Track retained version counts before/after releases and compare the mutex cost with read-copy-update assumptions.

steps: Derive demand accounting, signal ordering, cancellation and reentrancy limits; compare the original C subset to selected Reactive Streams rules without claiming interface or certification equivalence.
Implement explicit demand/terminal/delivering state, saturating unbounded arithmetic and callback ownership; construct a channel adapter that never delivers more items than requested.
checks: Emit with demand0 is EMPTY. Request1 then emit99 whose callback requests1 leaves demand1 without recursive delivery; emit7 consumes it. UINT64_MAX then request1 stays unbounded. Complete then error produces one terminal event; later emit is CLOSED. Cancellation prevents subsequent emits but does not establish cross-thread callback quiescence.

Enumerate request/emit/cancel/end traces, test zero and maximum demand, callback requests/cancellation and recursive emission. Reject emission without credit and repeated-terminal mutants. Independently account for requested versus delivered finite items, retain callback context through return and test that end requires no demand.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-OR-03: Which representation preserves the required ownership and evaluation contract with lower measured cost? Compare explicit checked state and direct operations versus composed wrapper/adapter representation. Seal prediction before measurements; compare identical admitted inputs, rejection effects, operation counts, allocation and layout, then explain counterexamples.

Derive disjoint number and integer bit partitions, pointer round-trip preconditions and negative decoding; classify portable arithmetic, implementation-defined pointer mapping and explicit IEEE-format assumptions.

Implement numeric NaN canonicalization, int32 boxing/unboxing and checked two-bit pointer tags from the exact contract. Build a discriminated-union alternative and a character-copy double bridge with verified format assumptions; never truncate a pointer into a payload.
checks: 0x7ff9000000000042 as numeric input canonicalizes to0x7ff8000000000000; int32 minimum round-trips as -2147483648; negative zero remains0x8000000000000000. A low-bit-misaligned pointer rejects without changing output.

Enumerate signed extrema and NaN payload collisions, signed zero, infinities, misaligned integer mappings and reserved bits. Reject missing-canonicalization and sign-loss mutants; compare integer decoding with Python integers and verify native pointer round trips only for admitted live objects.

steps: Derive deadline versus timeout semantics, cancellation precedence, parent lifetime and nonextension of inherited budget. Distinguish stopping admission from acknowledgement and rollback.

checks: Parent created at10 with budget10 expires20. A child at13 asking100 still expires20; at19 remaining is1 and at20 it is expired. Cancelling the parent makes the child CANCELLED. No borrowed storage becomes reclaimable solely because cancellation was requested.

Exhaust now0–16/budget0–16 across parent/child creation and every cancellation/finish permutation for two borrowers. Use mathematical min and arbitrary-precision addition as an oracle. Test UINT64_MAX edges and chain depth8/9. Compare Go Context documented cancellation and deadline behavior with the C runtime checks and caller lifetime discipline; never infer acknowledgement from an atomic flag.

steps: Derive bucket index, full due identity, list invariants and generation retirement. Prove why modulo bucket equality alone is insufficient across revolutions.
Implement bounded schedule/cancel/tick and a two-level cascade extension with no lost or duplicate expiries, explicit horizon, late tick and immediate timer policies.
checks: At now0 a delay5 timer maps to bucket1 but must not fire at tick1; it fires exactly at5. Cancelling generation1 then reusing that slot at generation2 makes the old ID STALE. Simultaneous due timers all appear in the returned mask, without invoking callbacks during linkage traversal.

Use an independent sorted map of absolute due times, not another wheel. Exhaust pairs of due1..16 and every cancellation point; verify back-links after each step. Add a delayed-clock jump that crosses three revolutions and either process all missed ticks or specify a bounded late-fire policy. Record the selected scheduler decision before measurement; historical paper VAX numbers are source observations only.

steps: Derive distinct health and capacity invariants, permit ownership, epoch identity and neutral-versus-backend-failure classification; explain why a failure window is not a concurrency bound.
Implement bounded admission/completion with generation and epoch exhaustion, including late old-epoch results and four-tick cooldown overflow retirement.
checks: With limit1, a second simultaneous admission returns BUSY even while CLOSED. Two classified failures open. An older outstanding success releases capacity but leaves the newer OPEN state unchanged. At cooldown equality one probe may enter, a second is BUSY, and successful probe closes. Repeated completion is STALE.

Enumerate admit/fail/succeed/neutral sequences through each finite generation. Test old admission before two failures, then a late success after OPEN. Check capacity and exactly-once release after every event. Use an original synthetic overload trace to demonstrate the missing-limit mutant permits excess work; the stale-epoch mutant reopens traffic after a declared trip. Observe counters/status only, not external service load.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-RZ-18: Which overload and retry policy preserves the telemetry effect/delivery contract under bounded resources? Compare reject before effect with explicit retry ownership versus commit into a durable bounded outbox then drain versus lossy/coalescing telemetry with an explicit weaker observation contract. Whether lost or repeated notifications are allowed, what survives reset, and which owner retains outstanding work determine admissibility before latency comparison.

Derive a composition contract with admission, effect commit, reply availability, notification enqueue, delivery and cleanup as distinct events. Account for every retained buffer, timer, permit and borrowed owner.

Implement the bounded service anchor using actual conc.channel and all required local IPC/reactor/fault adapters; preserve exactly-once notification for a new retained request and explicit replay/expiry semantics.
checks: A new delta2 request applies once and queues its ID. Flush to channel0 allows msg_select to observe that exact ID. Filling the four pending slots rejects the next request before changing receiver.total. A full/cancelled imported channel retains pending notifications. Cancellation after an admitted effect cannot make its already-reserved notification disappear.

For the public anchor, fill/drain the real MsgHub, close/cancel it and compare pending IDs with receiver records. Mutation1 commits after notification capacity is exhausted; mutation2 discards an item without channel acceptance. For the full integration, enumerate each acquisition/failure prefix and replay randomized seeded event traces with an independent total/effect ledger. Retain exact compiler/link dependencies and actual measured traces. Do not record a simulated timer observation as hardware/network latency.

steps: Before the main implementation, seal the design decision for LAB-RP-02: Choose the authority and commit boundary of your event log, snapshot and externally visible effects before seeing the failure campaign. Compare Immutable event authority with rebuildable projections and explicitly committed effects versus Snapshot authority with a versioned recovery log and explicitly stated lost-update/replay policy. Seal the selected invariant and crash-point predictions before implementation; compare recovery after each cut.

Distinguish immutable event history, a current projection, a retained snapshot root and durable storage. Derive why replay requires event-version and external-query assumptions, not merely a list of bytes.

Retain the actual PR-T70-07 learner artifact and its64node/3nodes-per-update contract. Prove16 appends use48nodes, every published root remains immutable and an interrupted failed append cannot advance count. Initialization requires no surviving borrowed roots; do not copy/relocate a live arena and interpret roots in another owner. Account for unpublished cells and allocation counters separately from reachable state. State a release/publication order for a future concurrent adapter.
checks: Append(3,7),append(3,9): prefix1 returns7 and prefix2 returns9. Inject each allocation ordinal1..3 on the next append: count stays2, used count is restored and prior roots still resolve. The17th append returns RP_FULL without consuming nodes.

Run replicated.log and the three allocation-cut assertions, compare every prefix against an independent key/value dictionary and rebuild into a fresh arena. Reject count-before-commit and latest-root-for-all-snapshots mutants. Inspect source/link dependencies to establish that the real imported HAMT is used. Separately implement the required codec.records/storage.pages adapter with short writes and crash schedules; the memory anchor does not validate that adapter.

steps: Separate query-model choice from delivery semantics. Establish exactly-once application only within one serialized projection and one retained immutable log identity; reject the stronger claim of exactly-once external effects.

Prove the invariant count=k implies exactly the first k events contributed once and applied[i].position=i+1. A 16-term int32 sum fits int64 on the declared target. Retain history for conflict checks rather than trusting a reused position from a new log. The caller must associate a projection with one log identity. Explain why a mutex around cursor alone is insufficient, and why an external email/file effect cannot become atomic with this state by naming it CQRS.
checks: Apply(1,0,7) twice yields total7,count1. Reuse position1 with8 conflicts; position3 before2 is a gap. Two synchronized threads each delivering values1..16 yield count16,total136;128 fresh concurrent runs test the adapter.

Run replicated.projection, including actual pthread schedules under GCC TSan when available. Kill duplicate-reapplication and gap-acceptance mutants with semantic assertions. Record mutex boundaries and model the crash point between query-state and cursor persistence. A TSan pass observes these executions only; it does not certify arbitrary effects or all schedules.

steps: Derive three different clock contracts: Lamport timestamps preserve happened-before in one direction, vectors characterize causality under fixed known membership, and HLC pairs retain a physical component without eliminating physical-clock assumptions.

Show two concurrent events with ordered Lamport timestamps, two incomparable vectors and every HLC equality case. Separate physical-clock closeness claims from the synchronization assumptions in Corollary1. On local overflow choose explicit failure; neither arbitrary sleep nor silently increasing physical time is equivalent. Outputs are ordinary C structs, so validity and per-replica serialization remain caller obligations.
checks: Lamport(2,8)=9. Vectors[1,0,0] and[0,1,0] are concurrent; receive at replica0 gives[2,1,0]. HLC local(10,2),remote(10,7),wall9 gives(10,8); wall11 on a subsequent local event resets logical to0. UINT32_MAX logical overflow fails unchanged.

Run replicated.clocks and independent exhaustive small HLC branch enumeration plus uint64/uint32 extrema. Kill ignoring-remote Lamport and incorrect equal-physical HLC-counter mutants. Build small message histories and derive causal relations from graph reachability before comparing clock outputs; timestamp ordering alone is not the oracle.

steps: Derive convergence from explicit componentwise joins and globally unique writer identities, and distinguish state merge from replaying operations. A last-writer register resolves an order chosen by the protocol, not necessarily real-time recency.

Prove idempotence, commutativity and associativity on admitted compatible states, plus inflation of each grow-only component. Explain why sum of received states double-counts retransmission, why finite overflow must reject, and why a reused writer identity with forked state violates the ownership model. For registers identify conflict cases outside the unique-event assumption and the total-order tie rule.
checks: Replica0 adds5; replica1 subtracts3. Merge yields2 and repeating the same merge remains2. Register(7,0,1) joined with(7,2,9) chooses9; another payload at(7,2) is a conflict. Adding UINT32_MAX to component5 fails unchanged.

Run replicated.counters; enumerate small component states and three-way merge permutations, including duplicate, reordered and dropped-then-retransmitted messages. Kill additive-state-merge and missing replica tie-break mutants. Show a counterexample for unchecked uint32 wrap and for independent writers sharing one replica slot.

steps: Explain add-wins observed removal through unique add identities, retained tombstones and idempotent delta joins. Distinguish a causally self-contained delta representation from arbitrary partial operations or unsafe tombstone collection.

Define membership as adds minus removed. Derive why a concurrent unobserved add survives removal and why an observed add cannot resurrect when its delta arrives again. Treat one writer per replica as a premise. The bounded delta carries exact tag tombstones, so remove-before-add delivery is representable; do not infer this for all causal CRDTs. Explain the delta-interval causal precondition from the paper and specify acknowledgment/stability requirements before reclaiming history.
checks: Replica0 adds value2; replica1 observes it. Replica0 removes while replica1 concurrently adds its own tag. Join retains value2. Removing after observing both tags and replaying either old add delta does not resurrect it. The ninth add by one replica fails without resetting its identity counter.

Run replicated.sets and enumerate two-writer add/remove/delivery traces against a mathematical tagged-set oracle. Include duplicate and remove-before-add delivery. Kill remove-all-possible-tags and omitted-tombstone-merge mutants. Inventory retained tags and show the exact full condition rather than silently dropping history.

steps: Separate stable sequence identity from transient visible position, and compare a bounded parent-tree sequence with context-dependent operational transformation. Pairwise insertion agreement is a necessary local property, not a complete OT correctness theorem.

Derive acyclicity from parent<id and closure from causal admission. Prove insertion-order-independent rendering for a fixed admitted node set, including descendants of deleted anchors. Explain that this original tree contract is RGA-inspired, not a claim to implement every detail of Specification19. For OT derive the two-branch diamond under distinct priorities and identify the state-vector/log context needed beyond it.
checks: Insert A(id1,parent0),B(id2,parent0),C(id3,parent1) in either admissible arrival order: render BAC. Delete id1: render BC, retaining descendant C. Two inserts at position0 with priorities1 and2 transform the higher-priority-number insertion to position1.

Run replicated.sequence; enumerate topological arrival orders and deletion subsets against a recursive tree oracle. Kill arrival-order sibling rendering and deleted-subtree omission mutants. Check full capacity, duplicate identity, missing dependency and output failure atomicity. Enumerate both paths of the two-insert OT diamond, then provide a three-operation context counterexample to an unjustified generalization.

steps: Derive a domain-separated Merkle root for an exact ordered leaf sequence, distinguishing hash equality under a collision assumption from identity authentication, availability or a proof that arbitrary bytes are well formed.

Derive padding across55/56/63/64/65-byte boundaries, uint32 modular arithmetic, round constants and endian conversion. Prove the tree shape for non-power-of-two counts and that a subtree comparison is meaningful only with the same position/range/domain. Account for hash collision and corrupt-peer assumptions; a matching root alone authenticates no sender and guarantees no retrievability.
checks: SHA256(empty)=e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855. Trees[1,2,3] and[1,2,9] differ only at bit2 (mask4); empty trees give mask0. Compare every count0..8 with a separately implemented Python hashlib construction.

Run replicated.merkle, standard empty/abc hash vectors, all padding boundaries and independent randomized hashlib differential cases. Kill omitted leaf-domain prefix and ignored right-child mutants. Inspect the generated code for the intended unsigned operations; benchmark nodes hashed versus full leaf comparison under equal correctness/security contracts.

steps: Distinguish a wire grammar from one canonical encoding and show why deterministic serialization under one binary is not a universal content identity. Derive portable signed ZigZag arithmetic without signed-left-shift assumptions.

For five-byte uint32 varints require the final payload<=15 and no continuation. Derive ZigZag using unsigned conversion/shift and a sign mask; decode odd values as -(value>>1)-1 to include INT32_MIN safely. Prove canonical decode/reencode idempotence and uniqueness for the admitted semantic map. Explain the tradeoff of rejecting duplicate fields compared with protocols that merge repeated occurrences.
checks: Bytes18 07 10 01 08 96 01 (hex) decode and canonicalize to08 96 01 10 01 18 07. 08 80 00 10 01 is rejected as nonminimal. ZigZag(-1)=1, INT32_MIN maps to UINT32_MAX, INT32_MAX maps to UINT32_MAX-1.

Run replicated.wire and an independent Python parser/encoder for boundary values and reordered field maps. Kill overlong-varint acceptance and incorrect negative ZigZag mutants. Enumerate every truncation, duplicate field, forbidden tag/wire type and output-capacity boundary; demonstrate two noncanonical orders producing the same canonical bytes.

requires_reasons.U-T01-03-03: Know how to build, run, bound and diagnose a small C component; no application library is implicitly linked.
requires_reasons.LAB-DO-14: Import persist.hamt: Typed arena HAMT with equality-checked collision buckets, snapshot-preserving update, separately verified deletion and explicit root lifetime/reclamation.
requires_reasons.U-T47-09-03: Import storage.pages: Existing byte-exact page format, caller serialization, complete-page I/O and explicit durability outcomes.
requires_reasons.U-T20-01-04: Import codec.records: Canonical record bytes independent of host layout; partial/malformed input cannot publish a partial record.
requires_reasons.LAB-HS-06: Import io.frame: Read a big-endian length-prefixed binary message from actual pipe writes and detect truncated EOF.
requires_reasons.LAB-HS-08: Import ipc.local: A real AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET child transforms a bounded binary request and replies.
requires_reasons.U-T32-02-02: Import testing.faults: Deterministic input/fault schedule, independent oracle and minimized first divergence.
requires_reasons.LAB-RP-16: Explicit project contract consumes the prior Field tags, minimal varints and canonical bytes capability.

steps: Implement the T20.03 functional-core boundary: explicit state and recorded input produce new state and effect requests, while an adapter owns effects. Demonstrate rollback equivalence without replaying externally visible effects or claiming that ordinary C enforces purity.

Prove determinism from complete state/input and defined unsigned arithmetic. Identify every effect boundary and distinguish speculative requests from committed presentation. Derive rollback of the HAMT used cursor after a failed second update while preserving old reachable roots; staged unreachable arena cells and allocation counters may differ. All arena users must be quiescent during the transaction, and roots from unpublished intermediate updates must never escape. Score overflow or invalid movement must not partially publish a state/effect.
checks: Initial(0,0,0,1),movement-1 gives position15,random1015568748,score0; next movement1 gives position0,score3. Eight inputs[1,1,0,-1,1,0,1,-1] produce score12. Replacing input4 with1 and replaying from the prior snapshot equals a fresh corrected fold. All six checkpoint failure cuts preserve the published root and used count.

Run replicated.replay and exhaustively compare all movement histories of length0..8 with a Python integer model; verify suffix rollback versus full replay. Kill omitted random-score contribution and failed second-update allocation-leak mutants. Build a synthetic effect adapter with idempotency key(timeline,tick) and injected failure; record one duplicate-effect counterexample if replay directly invokes the adapter. Inspect undefined symbols to confirm the core has no time/random/I/O dependency.

phases.title: Trustworthy small tools
phases.gate: Bounded record tool, checked input, explicit errors and repaired regressions.

phases.title: A portable toolbox
phases.gate: Bytes, containers, parsers, storage policies and algorithms shared by two consumers.

phases.title: Crossing execution boundaries
phases.gate: Actual files, pipes, processes and reset/UART adapters explain machine and OS boundaries.

phases.title: Responsive communicating systems
phases.gate: Telemetry and HTTP tolerate segmentation, overload, deadlines and shutdown.

phases.title: Original concurrent execution
phases.gate: Cooperative contexts, preemption, synchronization, scheduling and early protected execution.

phases.title: Programmable and durable components
phases.gate: Hosted VM and recoverable store reuse representations, allocation and fault harnesses.

phases.title: Multiple processors and ownership
phases.gate: SMP and AMP revalidate publication, cache/DMA visibility and reclamation separately.

phases.title: Composed protected systems
phases.gate: The same VM/store and protocol components operate across process and target boundaries.

phases.title: Architectural revision and defense
phases.gate: Changed requirements force a justified migration and new independent evidence.

phases.title: Advanced systems construction
phases.gate: Kernel, port, lifecycle, compiler, verification, I/O, security and numerical mechanisms with evidence scoped to each environment.

phases.title: Modern abstractions from first principles
phases.gate: Representation, ownership, failure and cost contracts compose across errors, values, generics, layout and dispatch.

phases.title: Modern execution, runtime and data models
phases.gate: Protocols, continuations, concurrency, object runtimes, resilience and replicated state withstand changed conditions.
